listenings.text: Good morning, everybody, this is your first officer speaking. We have started our descent into Perth and we will be on the ground in about twenty five minutes. Before we land, please fill in the card the crew gave you earlier. Australia is very strict about food, so read question nine slowly. Do you have any food, plants or animal products with you? If you do, write yes. Nobody gets in trouble for writing yes. People get in trouble for writing no when the answer is yes. And if you are not sure about something in your bag, write yes and ask an officer inside. Local time in Perth is six forty in the morning and it is already twenty two degrees. Welcome to Western Australia.

Morning. Passport, thanks. Where have you come from today? Brazil, all right. And how long are you staying in Australia? Six months. What are you doing here for six months, then? An exchange program, okay. Which school is that? And who are you staying with, a host family? Do you have their address on your phone? Good, that is all I need. Just two more. Did you pack this bag yourself? And is there anything in there that is not yours? Any food at all? Right. Look at the camera for me, and no smiling. That is you done. Enjoy your six months.

reading.rtitle: Before you land: notes for exchange students
paras: Your plane lands in Perth early in the morning. Follow the signs to arrivals, and then walk to passport control. An officer looks at your passport, asks you three or four questions and puts a stamp in it. Answer in a full sentence, look at her, and do not make jokes. She has done this four hundred times today.

On the plane the crew gives you a card. Fill in every line before you land. One question asks about food, plants and animal products. If you have anything like that, you declare it: you write yes. Nobody gets in trouble for writing yes. People get in trouble for writing no when the answer is yes.

After passport control you go down to baggage claim and take your bag off the belt. Then you walk to customs. If you wrote yes on the card, go to the red line. An officer opens your bag, looks at the food and usually takes it. That costs you two minutes. If you wrote no and there is an apple in your bag, it costs you more than three hundred dollars.

Quarantine is not about you, it is about the country. Australia is an island and it wants to stay clean. This part matters to you more than to most people: sand and dirt on your fins and inside your board bag are a quarantine problem too, so wash your board and your wetsuit at home before you pack them. Then the officer says welcome, and your host family is waiting on the other side of the door.
